description:
FILED s470 (Fable, 2026-09-05, evening) from the USER's question after #1188 (module FASL cache, BP, awaiting merge): "Aren't cached compiled Perl modules sensitive to changes in modules they load?  We could do it for CPAN modules, of course."

THE HOLE (pre-dates #1188; the .lisp transpile cache has it too).  A module A's TRANSPILE consults the modules it `use`s: `_extract_module_prototypes` / `_merge_module_prototypes` (Pl/Parser.pm ~9410/~9686) read B's prototypes (a `(&@)` makes a trailing block a block-form; a `()` prototype makes a bareword a TERM â #365) and its exports; so A's emitted Lisp encodes facts about B.  The cache path is A's absolute path + *pcl-cache-generation* (+ for fasls the runtime hash and SBCL identity â #1188); validity (`p-cache-valid-p`, runtime ~17014) compares A's OWN mtime against the cache file.  Nothing about B is in the key or the check: when B's prototypes/exports change, A's cached parse is silently stale.  The fasl adds compile-time consequences on top (whatever compile-file folds).

WHY IT IS TOLERABLE FOR INSTALLED CPAN MODULES: they change only on a reinstall; even then only their DEPENDENTS go stale, and `pcl --clear-cache` clears it.  For modules under development beside the program it is a silent-wrong trap.

FIX SHAPE (two halves):
 (1) DEPENDENCY MANIFEST â the transpiler already knows what it consulted: `pl2cl --module` writes beside the cached emission the list of (module path, content hash) it read prototypes/exports from (the seam is `_merge_module_prototypes`'s input list); `p-cache-valid-p` checks each entry's current hash at load; transitivity is free because each dependency is validated when IT loads.  Cheap; the same manifest feeds `pl2cl --manifest` (s470bm) as `depends`.
 (2) TRUST-CLASS POLICY (the USER's belt): cache fasls only for modules resolved from the INSTALLED @INC directories (perl's lib/site_perl/vendor_perl and PCL's own lib/); a module reached through `use lib`, `-I`, `PERL5LIB` pointing into a checkout, or the program's own directory gets the .lisp cache with the manifest check but NO fasl â or a fasl under a per-program key.  A `PCL_FASL_CACHE=all|installed|none` switch.

ACCEPTANCE: probe = program P uses A, A uses B with `sub blk (&@)`; cache warm; edit B to drop the prototype; P must re-transpile A (today it does not â reproduce that first, on the .lisp cache alone, then with #1188's fasl).  `Pl/t/module-fasl-cache-01.t` (BP) gains the rows.  No emission change; runtime + pl2cl; gate + the module-load companion files (op/require.t op/do.t op/inccode.t).


=== DONE (s470bw, 2026-09-06) ===
SHIPPED as `3df7b66`.  Both halves; NO emission change and no generation bump.

STEP 0 â THE HOLE, REPRODUCED FIRST, on BOTH cache layers.  P uses A2; A2 uses
B2, which declares `sub blk (&@)` and exports `zap`.  Warm the cache, then edit
B2 only (A2's own mtime never moves):
  perl                       PCL (base tree, .lisp cache AND fasl cache)
  base           CODE:1 ZAP|1   CODE:1 ZAP|1        (agree)
  prototype gone HASH:1 ZAP|1   CODE:1 ZAP|1        SILENTLY STALE
  export gone    CODE:1 zap|1   CRASH "Undefined subroutine &A2::zap called"
After the fix both edits re-transpile A2 on both paths.  `Pl::ProtoCache` alone
is NOT a second hole â probed: transpiling A2 twice across a B2 edit gives one
`lambda` then none, because its entries already re-resolve and re-stat every
dependency.  (The prototype row's post-fix answer is `:1`, not perl's `HASH:1`,
because of a SEPARATE pre-existing bug filed as #1285: a declared sub with no
prototype followed by a block gets the block's VALUE where perl builds an anon
hash.  The cache half is what this task fixes, and it re-transpiles.)

HALF 1 â THE DEPENDENCY MANIFEST.  ONE dependency walk exists in the compiler
(Pl::ProtoCache's frames, #560), so `pl2cl` brackets a whole transpile in one
OUTERMOST `begin_walk`/`end_walk` and `$Pl::LAST_WALK` is the transitive list of
every module and file whose prototypes/exports it read.  `pl2cl --deps FILE`
writes it beside the cached emission as `<key>.deps`; `p-cache-valid-p` â THE
one validity predicate, used for both the .lisp and the fasl â re-hashes each
entry at load.  MD5 of CONTENT, never an mtime (a `git checkout` restores an
old mtime).  No manifest, or one that does not parse â INVALID (rule 12).
Transitivity is free: B is validated when B loads.  The same list is
`pl2cl --manifest`'s `depends` (Pl::Manifest gained the key; one walk, two
consumers).  The 7-day age clause was REMOVED from p-cache-valid-p: it stood in
for the staleness the manifest now states directly, and it made "an untouched
module is a HIT" untestable.  p-cleanup-old-cache still prunes by write date.

HALF 2 â RULED BY FABLE (s471) AS TWO DIRECTORY LISTS, not the brief's
PCL_FASL_CACHE=installed|all|none word.  `PCL_COMPILE_DIRS` (PERL5LIB syntax,
`*` = all; UNSET = perl's installed library dirs + PCL's lib/) and
`PCL_NO_COMPILE_DIRS` (same syntax, WINS on any match, `*` = compile nothing);
`PCL_NO_FASL_CACHE=1` kept as the alias of the latter's `*`.  Entries are
realpath'd at CALL time and memoised on the raw env string, so a saved core
cannot bake in the builder's answer.  A module that is not compiled still gets
the .lisp cache and the manifest check.
  *p-core-inc-dirs* is NOT the default's source, MEASURED not assumed: it is
  pl2cl's own @INC, so `PERL5LIB=/tmp ./pl2cl prog.pl` emits /tmp into it â
  exactly the directories a developer edits in.  The installed set is
  Pl::ProtoCache::installed_dirs (%Config's six *libexp keys + PCL's lib/), the
  ONE classifier, whose verdict reaches the runtime in the manifest's `source`
  line.
Module entries also moved to <cache>/modules/ (ruling item 7 â free now,
because every pre-manifest entry is invalid anyway).

BARS.  Gate 213 files / 7359 rows, only the 13 pclxs xs rows (main: 213/7333;
+26 = this session's guard rows).  corpus-diff 9ee95f2 IDENTICAL over 111,
silent drops 5 unchanged; emission-ab --shapes over lib/ 28 SAME / 0 DIFF /
0 RCDIFF; ir-host-leak 31 symbols / 111 files (the standing number).  Full
sweep --jobs 4: GATE clean, TOTAL passing 18646 / 18646 (+0), 0 new / 0 fixed,
drops 5 = census, shortfall +0; its 4 UNSTABLE + 15 unverified rows reproduce
BYTE-FOR-BYTE on a `git archive 9ee95f2` extraction, so they are pre-existing
crash-file noise, measured rather than asserted.  Companion --jobs 1 over
op/require.t op/do.t op/inccode.t op/incfilter.t op/require_errors.t: identical
file-for-file to the same run on the base extraction, ROW DIFF 0/0/0/0.
Guards: Pl/t/module-fasl-cache-01.t 22 -> 42 (every fasl-path row now passes
PCL_COMPILE_DIRS='*', or the default would make "fasl build" and "fasl hit"
both the TEXT path and stop testing what they say), Pl/t/manifest-01.t 47 -> 53.
INVERSE-verified on the base extraction: 12 rows fail there, exactly the new
behaviour.  docs/ir-spec.md Â§9.2b is the normative statement #1262 cites.

FILED: #1284 (`pcl -I DIR` does not reach a MODULE's own transpile), #1285 (a
no-prototype sub followed by a block gets the block's value, not an anon hash).

=== MERGE BARS RE-TAKEN (s470bw resume, 2026-09-06) ===
Rebased onto main d65f4a7c and then fcf076f1 (s471b).  Gate 213 files / 7374
rows, only the 13 pclxs xs rows; corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 (silent drops
5); full sweep --jobs 4 GATE clean, TOTAL passing 18647 = baseline (+0), drops
5 = census, shortfall +0; companion --jobs 1 over op/aassign.t op/lc.t op/do.t
op/inccode.t op/incfilter.t op/require_errors.t equal to the snapshot file for

rows) -- the cache introduces no divergence; four rows differ from blessed and

subject: The module cache (.lisp AND #1188's fasl) is NOT invalidated when a module a cached module `use`s changes -- A's parse encodes B's prototypes/exports, but the key/validity check reads only A's own path+mtime; fix = a dependency manifest checked at load + a trust-class policy (fasls only for INSTALLED @INC modules, USER)
